Why the long comment, and calling it a hack?

This seems to be consistent with the documentation:
> If set to [code]Color(0, 0, 0, 0)[/code], no additional color is applied.

EDIT:
Ok I'm not sure what the condition should be. If you simply write it like now, the `else` has no effect.

> Ok I'm not sure what the condition should be. If you simply write it like now, the `else` has no effect.

I've looked into this and:
- `theme_cache.background_color` is a single color for the whole TextEdit.
- `line_background_color` is a per-line custom color. If a line has no custom color, then the default `Color(0, 0, 0, 0)` is stored in its per-line data.

So:
- `if (line_background_color != theme_cache.background_color)` check makes no sense, as these are completely unrelated values.
- `if (line_background_color != Color(0, 0, 0, 0))` means "if the line has a custom background color" which is an absolutely valid / not hacky check.

This if/else was added in #85054. The original intention was to make the error etc. more visible, as previously `line_background_color.a *= 0.6` was always done.

So I think the correct code would be something like:
```cpp
const bool line_has_custom_background_color = line_background_color != Color(0, 0, 0, 0);
if (line_has_custom_background_color) {
	// Make non-default background colors more visible, such as error markers.
	line_background_color.a = 1.0;
}
```
The `else` indeed makes no sense here, "hack comment" too.

Hey there. Good morning.

I wrote the long comment calling it a hack because I wasn't sure about the purpose of the previous implementation. I looked through the commit history and spent a lot of time looking through the previous code and where this property was used and I couldn't figure out why it was being matched against the Theme Cache.

Because of this I decided to keep my changes as minimalist as possible and change the erroring line. I'm not sure if the else statement triggers at all either, because if it did, we would get semi translucent black lines. I'm not sure what it is doing, but to be on the safe side I decided to keep it.

Anyway, I have an exam to write in a few hours, but once I'm free, here are the changes I will make:
- Remove redundant else statement 
- Remove long comment.

EDIT : Since we don't have that else statement anymore, we could code it in a branchless way, like this
`line_background_color.a = 1.0 * line_has_custom_background_color;`

I did it the if statement way. See my new commit. Let me know if you'd prefer this branchless solution instead.

Considering the nature of this code, it could give really small performance benefits to lower end systems. Not a whole lot, but every bit counts right?

The bool variable doesn't look necessary. It's used only once.
The branchless code could be written as `line_background_color.a = float(line_background_color != Color(0, 0, 0, 0))`, but it's probably less readable.
